name: nRF51822-QFAA-R
title: Bluetooth low energy and 2.4 GHz proprietary radio SoC with Arm Cortex-M0
summary: A single-chip 2.4 GHz radio and 16 MHz Arm Cortex-M0 microcontroller with 256 kB or 128 kB of flash and 16 kB of RAM, for Bluetooth low energy (with Nordic's S100 SoftDevices) and proprietary protocols at 250 kbps, 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps. It runs from 1.8 V to 3.6 V through an internal LDO, from 2.1 V to 3.6 V through an internal buck converter, or from an external 1.8 V rail. Peripherals include a 10 bit ADC, low power comparator, SPI, two-wire, UART, quadrature decoder, AES ECB/CCM, address resolver, RNG, timers and RTCs; the serial interface and quadrature decoder signals can be put on any of up to 32 GPIOs. It comes in a 6 x 6 mm QFN48 and a 3.50 x 3.83 mm WLCSP.
key_figures: 256 kB (QFAA, CEAA) or 128 kB (QFAB) flash; 16 kB RAM
2400 MHz to 2483 MHz GFSK, 250 kbps, 1 Mbps, 2 Mbps

circuits.title: QFN48 with internal LDO regulator
circuits.description: Reference circuit for the QFN48 part. VCC_nRF feeds VDD and AVDD and the internal LDO makes the core supply; DCC is left open. C7 and C11 sit at the two VDD pins, C9 at AVDD, C10 at DEC2 and C8 at DEC1. The 16 MHz crystal X1 sits across XC1 and XC2 with 12 pF load capacitors C1 and C2 to ground. L1, L2 and C3 form the differential-to-single-ended match: VDD_PA reaches ANT1 through L2 and ANT2 through L2 and L1, with C3 decoupling it; C5, C4, L3 and C6 complete the match into a 50 Ω single-ended antenna. The GPIOs, SWDIO/nRESET and SWDCLK are brought out as labelled signals with nothing else on them.

equations.name: Load capacitance, 16/32 MHz crystal
equations.expr: CL = (C1' × C2') / (C1' + C2'); C1' = C1 + C_pcb1 + C_pin; C2' = C2 + C_pcb2 + C_pin

where.CL: total load capacitance across the crystal terminals; it has to match the crystal's rated load
where.C1, C2: ceramic SMD capacitors from each crystal terminal to ground, chosen equal
where.C_pcb1, C_pcb2: board stray capacitance on each side; 0.5 pF each in the reference layouts
where.C_pin: pin capacitance of XC1 and XC2, 4 pF (16M and 32M XOSC tables)

equations.name: Load capacitance, 32.768 kHz crystal
equations.expr: CL = (C1' × C2') / (C1' + C2'); C1' = C1 + C_pcb1 + C_pin; C2' = C2 + C_pcb2 + C_pin

where.CL: total load capacitance across the crystal terminals; it has to match the crystal's rated load
where.C1, C2: ceramic SMD capacitors from each crystal terminal to ground, chosen equal
where.C_pcb1, C_pcb2: board stray capacitance on each side; 0.5 pF each in the reference layouts
where.C_pin: pin capacitance of XL1 and XL2, 4 pF (32k XOSC table)

operation.text: One die carries a 2.4 GHz transceiver, a 32 bit Arm Cortex-M0, flash, RAM and analog and digital peripherals. It runs Bluetooth low energy through Nordic's S100 series SoftDevices, which load separately from the application, and proprietary 2.4 GHz protocols such as Gazell. Variants: QFAA (QFN48, 256 kB flash), QFAB (QFN48, 128 kB flash) and CEAA (62-ball WLCSP, 256 kB flash), all with 16 kB RAM.

The Cortex-M0 executes Thumb-2 code (16 bit instructions plus some 32 bit ones) on a 3-stage pipeline, multiplies 32 bit values in one cycle and takes interrupts through the NVIC. CMSIS support exists, and code moves forward to Cortex-M3 parts.

Code, RAM, the factory (FICR, 0x10000000) and user (UICR, 0x10001000) configuration registers and the peripherals share one address space; code starts at 0x00000000, RAM at 0x20000000, APB peripherals at 0x40000000 and AHB peripherals at 0x50000000. Flash is programmed through the NVMC, either over SWD or by code running from the code area. RAM is split into two 8 kB blocks whose power is controlled separately by the POWER block.
The MPU can block readback of the whole flash or protect 4 kB blocks of it from writing and erasing. The readback lock byte lives in the UICR; block protection registers clear only on a chip reset.

System OFF is the deepest state; the chip leaves it through a reset or a GPIO, LPCOMP or pin wake-up, and RAM can be kept in up to two regions. In System ON each block (CPU, radio, peripherals) is independently in RUN or IDLE. Supervision covers power-on reset, brown-out reset and a power fail comparator with thresholds of 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 and 2.7 V.

Three supply arrangements: 1.8 V to 3.6 V through the internal LDO; 2.1 V to 3.6 V through the internal DC/DC buck converter feeding the LDO; and low voltage mode, 1.75 V to 1.95 V from an external regulator with DEC2 tied to VDD.

The buck converter steps the battery voltage down ahead of the linear regulator and needs three external parts (L4, L5, C12 in the reference circuits). It can be switched off near the bottom of its supply range so the LDO carries on alone, and it pauses by itself when only the low-current internal regulator is needed. From a 3 V coin cell it cuts peak battery current by roughly 30%.

The PPI ties one peripheral's events to another's tasks without the CPU: 16 programmable channels (0 to 15) and 12 channels with fixed endpoints (20 to 31), in 4 groups. Timer and GPIO tasks over PPI give PWM and timed outputs on any pin, limited by the 4 GPIOTE channels.

HFCLK comes from a 16 MHz or 32 MHz crystal, an external 16 MHz reference or the 16 MHz RC oscillator; the system clock is 16 MHz either way, and the radio needs the crystal. LFCLK comes from a 32.768 kHz crystal, an external 32.768 kHz reference, the 32.768 kHz RC oscillator or is synthesized from HFCLK. Oscillators start and stop automatically as blocks request them; software can hold one running to avoid start-up delay. Clocks exist only in System ON.

An AT-cut crystal in parallel resonance goes across XC1 and XC2 with equal load capacitors to ground. Its load capacitance, shunt capacitance, ESR and drive level must meet the 16M or 32M XOSC table. With a high load or shunt capacitance a crystal of lower ESR than the limit starts faster and draws less; a low load capacitance cuts both start-up time and current.

A 32.768 kHz crystal goes across XL1 and XL2 the same way. The 32.768 kHz RC oscillator needs no parts and holds better than ±250 ppm in stable temperature or with calibration every 4 s. The synthesized 32.768 kHz clock saves the crystal but keeps the high-frequency clock running, which raises average current.

After the oscillator is enabled it draws ISTART,XOSC while the crystal starts (tSTART,XOSC, set by the crystal), then a fixed debounce period passes before the clock is released; the two together make tSTART,X16M or tSTART,X32M.

Up to 32 I/Os on one port (31 on QFN48, 32 on WLCSP). Each pin has its own direction, drive strength, pull-up or pull-down, level-triggered wake-up and interrupt, and can carry any serial interface or quadrature decoder signal. Standard drive is 0.5 mA; at most 3 pins may use the 5 mA high drive.

Two-wire Serial Wire Debug runs through the Debug Access Port; together with Nordic's trace buffer it offers breakpoints, stepping and capture of instruction trace. SWDIO shares its pin with the active-low reset.

A pin reset needs nRESET low for at least 0.2 μs, or 100 μs during debug, with SWDCLK held low; reset during debug has to be enabled in the POWER block's RESET register. The supply has to rise from 0 V to 1.8 V within 60 ms for the power-on reset to work reliably.

2.400 GHz to 2.4835 GHz GFSK transceiver at 250 kbps, 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps, compatible on air with Bluetooth low energy, ANT, Enhanced ShockBurst and the nRF24L series. Output runs from -20 dBm to +4 dBm in 4 dB steps plus a -30 dBm whisper level; RSSI resolves 1 dB. Channels are set in 1 MHz steps, spaced 1 MHz at 1 Mbps and 250 kbps and 2 MHz at 2 Mbps; a ±60 ppm 16 MHz crystal is enough. EasyDMA moves packets to and from RAM, with dynamic payload length, on-the-fly AES CCM and an 8, 16 or 24 bit CRC with programmable polynomial and start value. Continuous transmission is limited to 16 ms with a crystal better than ±30 ppm and 4 ms with ±60 ppm.

TIMER0 (up to 32 bit) and TIMER1 and TIMER2 (up to 16 bit) run from HFCLK through a 4 bit power-of-two prescaler, each with 4 capture/compare registers and a counter mode. RTC0 (3 compare) and RTC1 (4 compare) are 24 bit counters on LFCLK with a 12 bit prescaler and a tick event for tickless RTOS use. The watchdog counts down on LFCLK and can pause while the CPU sleeps or the debugger halts it.

ECB does 128 bit AES block encryption in RAM through EasyDMA. CCM does AES-128 CCM authenticated encryption to IETF RFC 3610 and the Bluetooth rules, producing the 4 byte MIC, and can run in step with the radio so packets are encrypted before sending and decrypted on arrival. AAR resolves Bluetooth resolvable private addresses against up to 8 IRKs as packets arrive; generating such addresses is done with ECB. The RNG gives true random numbers from thermal noise with no seed.
Measures die temperature over -25 °C to 75 °C in 0.25 °C steps, ±4 °C.

SPI0 and SPI1 are masters with double-buffered data; chip selects are ordinary GPIOs. SPIS1 is a slave with EasyDMA, so transfers run while the CPU idles. All support SPI modes 0 to 3. TWI0 and TWI1 are I2C-compatible masters at 100 kbps and 400 kbps with clock stretching. The UART runs full duplex up to 1 Mbps with hardware CTS/RTS and parity. Each interface's signals can be put on any GPIO. Instances sharing an ID (SPI0/TWI0; SPI1/SPIS1/TWI1) share a base address.
Decodes quadrature signals from mechanical or optical sensors with input debouncing and an optional LED drive output; sample period (128 μs to 16384 μs) and accumulation are configurable.

10 bit incremental ADC with 8, 9 or 10 bit results, 8 inputs through a multiplexer, and adjustable input and reference prescaling. References are the internal 1.20 V or AREF0/AREF1. The ADC and LPCOMP share AIN0 to AIN7 and AREF0/AREF1, and only one of them can be enabled at a time.

In System ON the LPCOMP raises separate rising and falling events or reports the input level against its threshold, which is set as a fraction of the supply. Any analog input can be used, and it can wake the chip from System OFF or System ON.

4 channels turn pin changes into events, or drive pins from events, through PPI. Pin change detection on port 0 works in System ON and System OFF and adds no current when used for wake-up or interrupt.
The WLCSP die is sensitive to light, visible and near-infrared alike. The marking side carries a light-absorbing film; the product must shield the edges and ball side, by coating or otherwise.

Each electrical figure carries a test level from 1 (simulated, calculated or prototype-tested at nominal conditions) to 4 (every production part limit-tested at nominal conditions); N/A marks figures that are defined rather than tested.

The reference circuits suit a 50 Ω single-ended antenna and should be copied closely, in schematic and layout; changing the layout of the parts between ANT1, ANT2, VDD_PA and the antenna changes RF behaviour or the values needed. Use at least two layers with a ground plane; on boards of more layers, keep inner layers clear under the matching network. Decouple the supply right at the VDD pins with RF-grade capacitors, filter the chip's supply and route it apart from digital supplies, and keep supply runs short. Grounds, VDD connections and bypass capacitors sit as close to the chip as possible; VSS pins go straight to a top-side ground plane, or to a bottom plane through at least one via per VSS pin placed at the pad. Keep full-swing digital lines away from the crystal and supply lines and keep their capacitive load low. The QFN48 exposed pad goes to ground.
The matching network has to present about 15 + j85 Ω differentially to ANT1 and ANT2 at 2.4 GHz while matching the antenna, normally 50 Ω.
